body:
Fixes #133
Fixes #130
Fixes #131
Fixes #132

## Changes

### #130: Pages deploy retries transient failures without deploying twice
- New dependency-free local action `.github/actions/deploy-pages` (`deploy.mjs`, `index.mjs`, `action.yml`). It replaces `actions/deploy-pages@v5`.
  - It uses the same REST protocol: an OIDC token, `POST /repos/{repo}/pages/deployments`, polling with ×1.5 backoff capped at 30 s, an error budget of 10 polls, a 10-minute timeout followed by a cancel, a cancel on SIGINT/SIGTERM, and the `page_url` output. The status messages match upstream.
  - A transient HTTP 5xx, 429, lost connection or request timeout while creating the deployment is retried up to 3 times, 10 s and then 20 s apart.
  - Before each retry the action calls `GET .../pages/deployments/{sha}`. It adopts that deployment unless it is in a final failed state, so a response lost after the server created the deployment never leads to a second deployment of the same commit.
  - Any other 4xx fails at once, without a retry. The message includes the status, the `x-github-request-id`, the response body, and a hint: for 401/403 it names the `pages: write` / `id-token: write` permissions, and for 404 it links the Pages settings.
- `docs.yml`:
  - The Pages upload step has `id: pages-artifact`, and the build job outputs `pages-artifact-id`.
  - The deploy job runs `uses: $/.github/actions/deploy-pages` with `artifact_id: ${{ needs.build.outputs.pages-artifact-id }}`, so it publishes exactly that artifact.
  - The `NODE_OPTIONS: --disable-warning=DEP0040` workaround is removed. The action has no npm dependencies, so there is no bundled `punycode`.
- `.github/actionlint.yaml`: the self-repository `$/` exception now also covers the `deploy-pages` path.

### #131: link checker
- `links.yml` runs every Monday at 06:00 UTC (`schedule`).
- The new step "Name today's link cache" outputs `date -u +%F`. The cache uses `key: cache-lychee-<day>-<sha>` and `restore-keys: cache-lychee-<day>-`, so only a cache saved the same UTC day is restored. lychee accepts such a cache under `--max-cache-age 1d`, so `[WARN] Cache is too old` cannot occur.

### #132: npm lockfile security
- **glob GHSA-3g3m-2fjr-6pw4 / minimatch GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249:**
  - The artifact action now pins `glob` 14.0.3 (via the `archiver-utils` override) and `minimatch` 11.0.4 (direct dependency plus `"minimatch": "$minimatch"` override).
  - `npm audit` reports 0 vulnerabilities.
  - `@actions/glob` 0.7.0, the latest release, calls `Minimatch#matchOne`, which minimatch 11 removed. `files.mjs` therefore matches upload paths with minimatch 11 directly and keeps the `@actions/glob` rules:
    - one pattern per line, with `#` comments and `!` exclusions;
    - every file under a matched directory is included;
    - hidden entries and symlinks are skipped.
  - `experiments/find_files_differential.mjs` checks this: 42 cases gave output identical to the old `@actions/glob` implementation.
  - `dist/` is rebuilt, and the rebuild is reproducible.
- **Security workflow:** the new job "Audit npm Lockfiles" runs `scripts/audit-npm-locks.sh`. It runs `npm audit --package-lock-only --audit-level=moderate` for every tracked `package-lock.json`, and on failure prints a `::error file=…` annotation with how to fix it. The job is part of the Pipeline Status gate and runs on pushes, PRs and the weekly schedule.
- **Dependabot:** new `.github/dependabot.yml` with `github-actions` for `/` and `npm` for `/.github/actions/artifact`. Both run weekly with `cooldown: default-days: 7` and grouped updates.
- **Dependabot and `dist/`:** Dependabot does not rebuild `dist/`. "Verify committed action bundle" now fails with an explicit annotation listing the rebuild commands, and this is documented in `dependabot.yml` and `docs/ci-evidence.md`.

### Docs and changelog
- README ("Deploying API documentation", Lychee section) and `docs/ci-evidence.md` are updated.
- Changelog fragment: `changelog.d/20261102_issue_133_ci_reliability.md`.

## How to reproduce the original problems
- **#130:** with `actions/deploy-pages@v5`, a single HTTP 500 from `POST /pages/deployments` fails the job with no retry. `tests/deploy-pages.test.mjs` scripts exactly this with a mocked API.
  - Mutation check: with adoption disabled, 2 tests fail; with `attempts = 1`, 10 tests fail.
- **#131:** before this change, `restore-keys: cache-lychee-` restored a cache of any age, and lychee logged `[WARN] Cache is too old` and discarded it. `links.yml` also had no `schedule`.
- **#132:** `npm audit --package-lock-only` on the old `.github/actions/artifact/package-lock.json` reports the glob and minimatch advisories. `scripts/audit-npm-locks.sh` exits 1 on a fixture repository containing that lock.

## Tests
- `node --throw-deprecation --test tests/deploy-pages.test.mjs`: 28 tests, all passing, covering:
  - 500/502/503/504/429 retried with exactly one deployment created;
  - network errors and timeouts retried;
  - 400/401/403/404/409/422 failing on the first call, reporting the status and request ID;
  - retries exhausted after 3 attempts;
  - adoption of a queued, in-progress or succeeded deployment;
  - a new deployment when the earlier one failed;
  - every final state;
  - temporary states and poll errors;
  - backoff, the interval cap, cancel after too many errors, and cancel on timeout;
  - artifact ID validation;
  - `githubApi`, `oidcToken`, and `main` writing `page_url`.
- These tests run in the Workflows pipeline ("Test Pages deployment retries and refusals"). `tests/*.test.mjs` is added to its path filters.
- `node --throw-deprecation --test tests/artifact.test.mjs`: 21 tests, all passing, including the new `findFiles` semantics test and the lockfile version assertions.
- `tests/test_issue_133_workflows.py` covers:
  - the build output, the deploy wiring, and the action interface with no dependencies;
  - the weekly schedule and the UTC-day cache key/restore-keys;
  - the npm-audit job and its gate;
  - the audit script listing every tracked lockfile;
  - the Dependabot ecosystems, directories, weekly interval and cooldown;
  - the stale-bundle error;
  - patched lockfile versions.
- Updated `tests/test_issue_118_workflows.py`: the cache key test, and the DEP0040 test is replaced by an assertion that no `NODE_OPTIONS` remain.
- Updated `tests/test_workflows.py`: the deploy-pages pin and the checkout count (27).
- Local checks:
  - actionlint 1.7.12 (the pinned image) is clean.
  - zizmor 1.30.1 (regular and pedantic, as in CI) reports no findings.
  - shellcheck 0.11.0.1 is clean.
  - `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass.

## Notes
- Adoption identifies a deployment by commit SHA (`pages_build_version`), which is what the Pages API's `GET /pages/deployments/{sha}` exposes. Adoption is only attempted on a retry within the same job, so the adopted deployment is normally the one the lost response created. The API cannot tell apart a deployment of the same commit that an earlier run created and that has not failed; such a deployment would also be adopted, and it publishes a site built from the same commit.
- The two moderate Dependabot alerts GitHub reports on `main` are the glob/minimatch advisories that this PR fixes.
title: fix(ci): retry Pages deploys, schedule the link checker, audit npm locks

body:
Fixes #128

## Changes
- `.github/actions/artifact/package.json`: scoped `overrides: { "archiver-utils": { "glob": "13.0.6" } }`. `archiver-utils/file.js` only calls `glob.sync(pattern, options)`, which glob 13 retains. It was the only `glob` consumer in the lock, so no other consumer is affected. Install warnings are not hidden.
- Regenerated `package-lock.json` and the ncc bundle `dist/index.mjs` (`licenses.txt` unchanged: glob stays ISC).
- New test in `tests/artifact.test.mjs`: checks that the lock contains only `glob@13.0.6` and no deprecated packages, and checks archiver-utils include/exclude/dot/filter matching and deterministic ZIP output.
- Changelog fragment.

## Verification
- `npm ci` with the old lock prints `npm warn deprecated glob@10.5.0`. With the new lock it prints no warnings, and `npm ls glob` shows `glob@13.0.6 overridden`.
- `experiments/archiver_glob_probe.cjs` produced identical `file.expand` results and an identical archive SHA256 (`276f6eb1…`) under glob 10 and glob 13.
- `node --throw-deprecation --test tests/artifact.test.mjs`: 20/20 tests pass. The existing hosted artifact round-trip CI job is unchanged.

## Additional CI fix
The Audit Workflows (zizmor) check started failing on `main` because of the new advisory GHSA-5xjx-3w67-w9x9 against `pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish` <= 1.14.2. Pinned v1.14.3 (`7245906f`) in `release.yml`. All checks now pass.

This PR addresses all six issues in #126 across every affected workflow and helper. Artifact transport failures now receive bounded retries without repeating validated tests; CodeQL findings fail the aggregate Security gate; failed link checks require valid evidence; release notes retain fenced examples.

| Issue | Implementation and verification |
| --- | --- |
| #120 | A bundled JavaScript action uses the pinned artifact SDK, three transport attempts with backoff, permanent-error refusal and lost-finalize reconciliation. All diagnostic, release, documentation and Pages artifact operations use it. Nineteen injected-error/file tests cover recovery, exhaustion, permanent failures, stale evidence and Pages packaging. |
| #121 | Both CodeQL languages inherit `CODEQL_ACTION_DIFF_INFORMED_QUERIES: 'false'` for init and analyze. All configured queries remain enabled. Both hosted analyses completed on a 341-file diff without diff-limit warnings. The temporary 301-file fixture was removed with a separate revert, preserving history. |
| #122 | Analyze writes local SARIF while retaining normal Code Scanning upload. A dependency-free gate rejects findings of every severity, malformed/missing reports and failed invocations across every file/run. Reports upload even after failure. Nineteen CLI cases cover the gate. |
| #123 | Missing, unreadable, empty or malformed reports from a failed lychee process return nonzero and `all_archived=false`. The final independent live-link gate remains enforced; archive suggestions cannot authorize broken links. Subprocess regressions require no network access. |
| #124 | Exact release headings are recognized outside matching backtick/tilde fences. Extraction preserves CRLF, body indentation, examples and subsequent subsections; missing entries fail explicitly. Regression cases first reproduced the truncation and example-only target bugs. |
| #125 | Every download bypasses the deprecated extractor with SDK raw downloads, mandatory SHA-256 verification and a validated Python ZIP extractor. Twelve subprocess cases cover traversal, symlinks, corrupt archives and nested/empty/binary files. The hosted round trip treats deprecations as errors and compares every byte, including Pages tar content. |

The complete requirement inventory, alternatives, upstream research and verification plan are in [experiments/issue_126_plan.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/blob/issue-126-89f22b11c0b0/experiments/issue_126_plan.md). [docs/ci-evidence.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/blob/issue-126-89f22b11c0b0/docs/ci-evidence.md) describes operation and maintenance. All six issues required changes; none were deferred or treated as already resolved.

Reproduction:

- Before the Python fixes, the new missing-report and fenced-changelog regressions produced 18 failures; the focused suite then passed all 42 cases.
- Before the local SARIF gate, its CLI/workflow regressions failed; the implemented gate passes the rejection/acceptance cases.
- `node --max-old-space-size=128 --pending-deprecation --throw-deprecation experiments/reproduce_artifact_buffer.mjs` reproduces upstream DEP0005 with two bytes and no credentials after installing the pinned action dependencies. Upstream [download-artifact #490](https://github.com/actions/download-artifact/pull/490) remains open, so this PR uses the documented raw-download workaround.

Local validation: **545 passed, 1 existing skip**; 19 Node tests passed. Ruff lint/format, mypy, file-size and changeset checks, actionlint, both zizmor modes, ShellCheck, Sphinx with warnings as errors, and npm audit (zero vulnerabilities) passed. A changelog fragment prepares the automatic release. Hosted verification:

- [Large-diff Security run](https://github.com/link-foundation/python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/40959801018): both Analyze steps completed with normal Code Scanning upload and no diff-limit warnings. The new local Python gate caught four existing badge substring findings, preserved SARIF, and correctly failed the aggregate Security gate. The shared release helpers now parse exact URL hosts, following [CodeQL guidance](https://codeql.github.com/codeql-query-help/python/py-incomplete-url-substring-sanitization/); six new regressions failed before this correction and all ten badge cases now pass. No query suppression or finding exception was added.
- [Hosted artifact regression](https://github.com/link-foundation/python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/40959801016/job/123749285519): all 19 Node tests and bundle reproducibility passed. Nested/binary/empty files and Pages tar contents survived upload/download byte comparisons with `NODE_OPTIONS=--throw-deprecation`, matching SHA-256 digests and no DEP0005.
- Real SARIF replay: a clean template Python report exits 0; downstream analysis 2049967568 exits 1 with all 50 findings, corroborating #122's additional evidence.
- **Final code commit `68a0cce9cd645ff4ed318bd9d895ea73191e765e`: all five workflows passed.** [Security](https://github.com/link-foundation/python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/40962459171), [Workflows](https://github.com/link-foundation/python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/40962459261), [CI/CD Pipeline](https://github.com/link-foundation/python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/40962459151), [Docs](https://github.com/link-foundation/python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/40962459470), and [Broken Link Checker](https://github.com/link-foundation/python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/40962459313).

CI selection, preflight diagnostics, and release gates currently miss failures or report misleading results. This change implements all 14 issues in #118 together, with reproducing tests and a patch changelog fragment.

## Changes and regression coverage

| Issue | Result | Verification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #104 | Exempt only the authenticated `dependabot[bot]` PR author from fragments; branch names grant no exemption | Validator CLI identity/spoofing tests and workflow wiring |
| #105 | Restore `queue: max` on both release writers, preserving non-cancellation | Workflow tests and bounded actionlint positive/negative controls |
| #106 | Scan the repository directory with Markdown/HTML extensions and existing exclusions; update every checkout/setup-python action to v7 | Workflow invariants, offline lychee scan, hosted link check |
| #107 | Shell and JSON changes activate code checks; excluded directories still take precedence | Both layouts and push/PR classifier tests |
| #108 | Decode PyPI 422 publisher errors, identify owner/repository/workflow/blank environment, and link to existing-project or pending-publisher setup | Local HTTP tests for both publisher codes, project existence, malformed JSON, uncertain errors, and token secrecy |
| #109 | Use mypy `extra_checks` without the deprecated option | Configuration test and mypy run |
| #110 | Authenticate the pedantic zizmor pass with the job's read-only token | Workflow assertion and authenticated regular/pedantic scans |
| #111 | Fail the dist upload immediately if no artifacts exist; enforce the same policy on every critical upload | All-workflow invariant |
| #112 | Probe dependency graph availability; warn/skip on PRs when disabled, fail main/scheduled runs with exact administrator instructions; retry uncertain failures | Fake-gh enabled/disabled/rate-limit/network/recovery tests and actual Security CI |
| #113 | Both release paths wait for docs/changelog/Docker checks and reject failures/cancellations; default manual bump to patch; persist lychee cache and failure report | Dependency/condition, input-default, cache, and artifact tests |
| #114 | Suppress only DEP0040 on the Pages deployment step, with an upstream removal note | Node test verifies another deprecation remains visible |
| #115 | Print the preflight verdict; add pinned standalone ShellCheck to CI/pre-commit, shell path triggers, and the terminal gate | All summary verdicts and tracked-shell lint |
| #116 | Require a strictly elapsed deadline for execution, TERM grace, and KILL waits | Aligned clock-boundary reproduction, deadline equality, and existing process-tree cleanup tests |
| #117 | Every terminal gate resolves `refs/pull/<n>/head` on the base repository and fails closed when lookup is inconclusive | Real Git fixtures for colliding fork names, absent branches, superseded/current heads, and unreachable remotes |

The dependency graph probe uses the comparison API as requested in the latest #112 feedback. Only a non-rate-limit HTTP 403 means disabled; other failures become unknown after retries. An enabled graph still runs dependency-review-action normally, so vulnerability findings remain blocking. No repository setting or publishing credential is changed by this PR.

The actionlint exception matches only the documented `queue` concurrency diagnostic until rhysd/actionlint#654 ships. Other unknown keys still fail, demonstrated by `experiments/reproduce_actionlint_queue.py`.

## Reproduction and validation

New regression tests failed against the original implementation before fixes. For example, a 1.4-second command started near a clock boundary was killed under a two-second budget; it now completes. Current fork heads could previously be excused using the base repository's `main`; exact PR refs now distinguish a superseded run from an unexplained cancellation.

Run the regressions with:

```sh
pytest tests/test_issue_118_workflows.py tests/test_detect_code_changes.py \
  tests/test_validate_changeset.py tests/test_preflight_credentials.py \
  tests/test_check_dependency_graph.py tests/test_check_pipeline_status.py \
  tests/test_run_with_budget_warning.py
python experiments/reproduce_actionlint_queue.py /path/to/actionlint
```

Local verification:

- Complete suite: **485 passed, one existing multi-language-layout skip**, 100% package coverage.
- Focused regressions: **238 passed**, same skip; final workflow/metadata checks also pass.
- Ruff lint/format, mypy, file-size and required-document checks, ShellCheck, and secretlint pass.
- Warning-fatal Sphinx build, wheel/sdist build, and Twine validation pass.
- Actionlint 1.7.12 with ShellCheck passes; documented `queue` is accepted and unknown `queue-size` is rejected. The native binary was used because this container cannot start Docker under its cgroup layout.
- Both authenticated zizmor personas report no findings. Lychee 0.24.2's offline directory scan reports zero errors and no missing-input warning.

All five hosted workflows passed on commit `467e4c82bd8d5d7a6943cdcaf52cf90d85872427` (runs created 2026-10-24 06:24:07 UTC): [CI/CD Pipeline](https://github.com/link-foundation/python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/40070060057), [Security](https://github.com/link-foundation/python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/40070060099), [Workflows](https://github.com/link-foundation/python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/40070060073), [Docs](https://github.com/link-foundation/python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/40070060085), and [Broken Link Checker](https://github.com/link-foundation/python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/40070060072). Python 3.13 also reports **485 passed, one existing skip, 100% package coverage**. The dependency graph probe found the graph enabled and the real dependency review passed. The online link scan checked 51 links with zero errors. Publishing and Pages deployment retain their existing event/settings gates.

The documented local zizmor scan used `.github/workflows`, so it missed findings in `.github/dependabot.yml` that the CI action audits with its default repository input. Change the regular reproduction command to scan `.` and explain that it includes Dependabot configuration when present. The existing version, policy and confidence filters remain aligned with CI.

Add a regression test that parses the documented command and verifies its input includes `.github/dependabot.yml`. Add a reusable experiment with one npm Dependabot update to demonstrate the missing cooldown finding and its seven-day fix. A changelog fragment prepares the change for the existing automatic version bump.

### Reproduction and regression

```sh
pip install zizmor==1.30.1
python experiments/reproduce_zizmor_scope.py
pytest tests/test_workflows.py::test_zizmor_reproduction_covers_dependabot
```

The experiment verifies all three states with the pinned CLI and the repository policy:

- `.github/workflows` without a cooldown: exit 0, missing the finding.
- `.` without a cooldown: exit 13 with `dependabot-cooldown`.
- `.` with `cooldown: default-days: 7`: exit 0.

The regression test failed against the original command and passes after the change. The experiment uses a temporary repository and offline scanning.

### Validation

- Full local suite: **365 passed, 1 skipped** (multi-language layout only); **100%** shipped-source coverage.
- Ruff lint/format, mypy, file-size limits, required-document checks, and committed changelog validation: passed.
- Pinned actionlint Docker image with shellcheck, Secretlint 13.0.7, zizmor regular and pedantic scans, and the documented pipx command: passed.

All four GitHub Actions workflows passed on commit `49c993488da458de87e42de3ae796a1cfb1f17a5`: [CI/CD](https://github.com/link-foundation/python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/38041043556), [Workflows](https://github.com/link-foundation/python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/38041043561), [Security](https://github.com/link-foundation/python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/38041043581), and [Links](https://github.com/link-foundation/python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/38041043573). Replacing a pending changelog fragment with a similar new fragment previously failed with “No new changelog fragment”: Git paired the files as a rename at its default 50% similarity threshold, and the additions filter discarded the replacement.

The additions diff now uses `--find-renames=100%`, so replacements with different content are validated as new fragments. Unchanged moves continue to be excluded, and source paths retain `--no-renames` so removals and moves out of source directories remain visible.

### Reproduction and regression coverage

`test_replacement_fragment_is_validated` creates an isolated Git history, changes source code, deletes `changelog.d/old.md`, and adds `changelog.d/new.md` with the same frontmatter and a different description. It confirms Git's default diff classifies the pair as a rename before running the validator.

The test covers both root and `python/` layouts, with valid and empty descriptions. All four cases failed before implementation because the validator detected zero additions. After the fix, valid replacements pass and malformed replacements fail content validation. The existing inherited-fragment tests verify unchanged moves remain rejected. Fixture subprocesses retain their 15-second limits.

```bash
pytest tests/test_validate_changeset.py -k replacement_fragment -vv
pytest tests/test_validate_changeset.py -vv
pytest --cov=src --cov-report=term
python scripts/validate_changeset.py --base-ref origin/main --head-ref HEAD --verbose
```

### Validation

- Changeset suite: **70 passed, 1 skipped** (expected layout-specific skip).
- Full local suite on Python 3.14: **364 passed, 1 skipped**, with 100% shipped-source coverage.
- Ruff lint/format, mypy, file-size limits, required documentation, committed-fragment validation, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Updated fragment documentation and added a changelog fragment to prepare the next release through the existing version-bump/fragment collection workflow.

All three triggered workflows passed on final commit `527124ef49a9fa2ece5463bd44ea3c2738e6a265`: **17 passing checks and five expected release-job skips**.

- [CI/CD Pipeline](https://github.com/link-foundation/python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/37661461497): changelog validation, lint, documentation checks, Python 3.13 tests (**364 passed, 1 skipped**), package build, and aggregate status passed.
- [Security](https://github.com/link-foundation/python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/37661461489): dependency review, resolved dependency audit, CodeQL, and aggregate status passed.
- [Broken Link Checker](https://github.com/link-foundation/python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/37661461584): all 51 link checks and aggregate status passed.

All run head SHAs match the final commit. Runs started at 2026-10-07 17:44:56 UTC, after the 17:44:48 UTC commit. Final logs are preserved locally in `ci-logs/`. Docs and workflow-audit workflows were outside this change's path filters. The default branch is included, the full GitHub diff has been reviewed, and the working tree is clean.

body:
Checkout hints obscured CI output, the workflow audit hid 22 template-injection findings, and a delayed PyPI release could leave every later release attempt failing on duplicate uploads. This change applies the checkout policy everywhere, audits those findings, and resumes publication whenever either the PyPI version or its published GitHub release is missing.

### Changes

- Configure Git before checkout in docs, security and workflow validation, with a policy regression covering every checkout workflow.
- Pass layout and release metadata through environment variables in every shell step. Use zizmor-action v0.6.4 with one shared zizmor 1.30.1 pin and a low-confidence regular audit; retain the pedantic security audit.
- Pin Secretlint and its preset to matching 13.0.7 versions.
- Check exact PyPI and GitHub release artifacts in automatic and manual releases for both root and `python/` layouts. Skip duplicate files in both publish actions and the standalone Twine publisher; preserve published GitHub releases and publish existing drafts during recovery.
- Wait up to 600 seconds for the exact PyPI version before the installation smoke test, with bounded requests, optional retry tracing and an actionable partial-success timeout message.
- Exclude both experiment directories through a wired CodeQL config. Add the commented `.lycheeignore` template and limit GitHub link requests to concurrency 2 and a one-second interval while preserving the existing failure/recovery gate.
- Add documentation and a changelog fragment, which prepares the next release through the existing version-bump/fragment workflow.

The [requirement-by-requirement analysis](https://github.com/link-foundation/python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/blob/issue-98-ebe758ce06fc/experiments/issue_98_analysis.md) lists every parent/sub-issue requirement, alternative solutions, selected plans, original log evidence, official online sources and related implementations. All listed issues were present; none needed an already-resolved exception.

### Reproduction and regression coverage

Before the fix, zizmor 1.30.1 at low confidence reported all 22 injections; the new workflow policies failed 11 cases, and GitHub release recovery tests failed twice. Original checkout-hint logs were downloaded and inspected. The old tag gate suppresses a missing release when a tag exists and republishes an already-uploaded version when no tag exists.

```bash
python experiments/reproduce_partial_release.py
pytest tests/test_issue_98.py tests/test_check_release.py tests/test_create_github_release.py
pytest --cov=src --cov-report=term
```

Fixes #93

Source-changing PRs now return exit 1 unless they add a valid changelog fragment. The local script and CI share the same validator, comparing the verified PR head with its Git merge base rather than accepting fragments inherited from the base branch.

## Changes

- Verify both refs and their merge base; missing refs, unrelated histories, and Git failures fail validation without a fallback comparison or network fetch.
- Count only committed, top-level `changelog.d/*.md` additions using `--diff-filter=A`. Existing, modified, renamed, untracked, instruction, and template files cannot satisfy the gate.
- Validate every added fragment's content from the head commit. Require a visible, recognized category and a description beneath it; commented templates and empty descriptions fail.
- Preserve the existing `src/`, `tests/`, and `scripts/` source scope and documentation/example/experiment exemptions. Support both root and `python/` project layouts.
- Replace the workflow's separate shell check with the validator, supplying base/head SHAs through environment variables and retaining full-history checkout. The validation job no longer needs to install Scriv; Scriv remains the fragment generation and collection tool.
- Document local invocation and add optional `--verbose` Git diagnostics, off by default.

The changelog fragment prepares the next release. The numeric version remains `0.1.0`, following the existing release workflow, which bumps the version and collects fragments automatically.

## Reproduction and regression coverage

Before the fix, changing `src/code.py` with no fragment returned success. A pre-existing valid fragment also satisfied the script regardless of whether this PR added one. The initial regression suite failed against that implementation before the fix was written.

Run the smallest regression for both supported layouts:

```bash
pytest tests/test_validate_changeset.py -k source_change_without_added_fragment_fails
```

`tests/test_validate_changeset.py` uses isolated, offline Git repositories to cover additions, inherited/modified/renamed fragments, removals, diverged base history, unavailable refs, unrelated histories, failed diffs, committed versus working-tree contents, explicit PR heads, shell-like ref text, invalid content, and existing exemptions. Subprocesses have finite 15-second test limits. Workflow regression assertions verify that CI calls this same implementation with the PR SHAs.

Local validation after committing:

```bash
python scripts/validate_changeset.py --base-ref origin/main --head-ref HEAD --verbose
```

This passes with the newly added fragment in this PR. Local checks also passed:

- Full pytest suite with coverage: **303 passed, 1 skipped** (the root-layout instance of a multi-language-only test); package coverage **100%**.
- Ruff lint and formatting, mypy on `src/`, file-size check, and `git diff --check`.
- Sphinx build with warnings treated as errors.
- CI-pinned actionlint Docker image (v1.7.12), including its bundled shell checks.
- CI-pinned zizmor 1.29.0 regular and high-severity/high-confidence pedantic checks.

## Hosted validation

All four triggered workflows passed on `6beccac45b588d2bc278abc881b58dafccc970e6`. Their runs started at 2026-10-07 01:22:15 UTC, after the 01:21:46 UTC commit:

body:
Fixes #89
Fixes #90
Fixes #91

All 26 active Ubuntu runner aliases are pinned to Ubuntu 24.04. The link re-check now retries cached and fresh 429/5xx responses, verifies throttled GitHub blob/tree links through the authenticated Contents API, and keeps final failures visible when other links recover.

## Requirements, alternatives, and implementation

| Issue | Requirement | Solution and verification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #89 | Prevent the announced Ubuntu 26 migration from changing inherited CI environments. | Replace all 26 `ubuntu-latest` values across docs (3), links (2), release (14), security (4), and workflows (3), including the Docker Linux runner matrix, with `ubuntu-24.04`. Update affected assertions and synthetic workflow fixtures. Existing versioned ARM64/macOS values remain supported. |
| #89 | Reject floating runner aliases and make future OS migration deliberate. | A regression scans both `.yml` and `.yaml` workflows, skips comment lines, and rejects Ubuntu, Windows, and macOS `-latest` aliases. README documents reviewed versioned-label upgrades. |
| #90 | Retry 429 and every 5xx, including lychee `Error (cached)`; retain transport retries. | Parse numeric markers and `Rejected status code` details separately from the fact that a host answered. Retry 429 and 500–599 plus unanswered HTTP URLs. Tests cover numeric/cached reports, generic ERROR markers, and all representative transient codes. |
| #90 | Back off between requests without exceeding the existing job budget. | Repair the old loop's missing wait; use exponential delays starting at the existing configurable 2 seconds and capped at 30 seconds. Stop starting requests when the 240-second budget expires and reduce network timeouts to remaining budget. Tests use a fake clock to prove scheduling, capped delays, budget expiration mid-round and persistent-outage behavior. |
| #90 | Fall back to authenticated Contents API GET for GitHub blob/tree pages. | Map exact HTTPS `github.com` file/directory URLs to the documented endpoint with encoded path/ref. Supply `GITHUB_TOKEN` to the workflow step; send it only to the fixed API host and disable API redirects. Only API 200 recovers a throttled page; API transport/status failures leave the original URL pending. Tests cover mapping, authentication, missing tokens, redirect policy, other hosts, and API errors. |
| #90 | Keep 4xx except 429 final; do not hide outages with accepted 503s or ignore rules. | Existing 404 behavior remains. No accept/ignore configuration changes. Mixed final/recovered reports cannot set `all_recovered=true`; conflicting final entries cannot enter recovered URLs; duplicates are deduplicated. Stale recovery files are cleared on a new report. Recovered URLs still bypass the archive lookup, while the existing fail-safe workflow gates remain. |
| #90 | Apply the changed semantics consistently. | Update workflow step name/comment, script documentation/messages, archive wording, README and workflow assertions. Add optional `RECHECK_VERBOSE=true` attempt diagnostics, off by default. |
| #91 | Read every listed issue and comments, implement both in one PR, and close all issues individually. | Read #89/#90/#91 and all issue/PR discussion/review comment types (empty at investigation). Both issues reproduced and are fully addressed here; the three separate closing references above close them on merge. |

The changelog fragment prepares the next release. The template remains at `0.1.0`: its release workflow collects fragments and performs the numeric version bump, as in recent merged PRs.

## Reproduction and regression tests

Before implementation, `pytest tests/test_issue_91.py` failed all nine initial cases: the workflow scan found floating Ubuntu labels, each transient response stopped retries, no backoff occurred, and a cached 503 never entered the recovered file. The existing gate also ignored final report entries when deciding whether every retried link had recovered; regression coverage now prevents that false pass.

`tests/test_issue_91.py` adds deterministic unit tests and a real local-HTTP/subprocess report replay. Existing connection-reset, 404, archive filtering and workflow-gate tests remain in place. The test suite runs in the existing CI test job.

Local verification:

- Full `pytest`: 237 passed.
- `ruff check .` and `ruff format --check .` passed.
- `mypy src/`, file-size checks and `git diff --check` passed.
- Sphinx build with warnings treated as errors passed.
- CI-pinned `rhysd/actionlint` v1.7.12 Docker image passed.
- CI-pinned zizmor 1.29.0 regular and high-severity/high-confidence pedantic passes reported no findings.

## Research and possible components

- [GitHub's runner-image announcement](https://github.com/actions/runner-images/issues/14748) specifies October 19–November 19, 2026 and recommends the `ubuntu-24.04` label. A versioned label directly solves the OS migration; actionlint validates workflow syntax, while the regression enforces the repository's label policy.
- [GitHub's Contents API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/repos/contents#get-repository-content) documents file/directory lookup and the `ref` parameter. The [REST rate-limit documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/using-the-rest-api/rate-limits-for-the-rest-api) shows that authenticated requests have a larger budget, but the API is still rate-limited; API failure therefore never proves a link healthy.
- [urllib3 Retry](https://urllib3.readthedocs.io/en/stable/reference/urllib3.util.html#urllib3.util.Retry) supplies status lists, exponential backoff and redirect credential handling. [Tenacity](https://tenacity.readthedocs.io/en/latest/) supplies general retry predicates, wait strategies and stop policies. Either could support a larger client, but neither supplies this report parser, Contents API mapping or recovered-file/gate protocol. Extending the standard-library implementation avoids adding an installation dependency to the CI recovery step.
- [lychee's CLI options](https://lychee.cli.rs/guides/cli/) already provide retries and acceptance configuration. Accepting 503 or ignoring GitHub would hide real failures; neither is used. The Python change follows the recovery approach in [hive-mind PR #2430](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/pull/2430).

Slash-containing refs must be percent-encoded in their URL segment for the API fallback; ambiguous unencoded refs are not guessed. Network timeouts bound socket operations, while the workflow's existing ten-minute job cap remains the outer limit. Tests simulate throttling deterministically rather than generating request bursts against GitHub.

## Hosted CI

All five workflows passed on `f615b43bfea151f0fda001eff5d323be858c7e34`; their runs started at 2026-10-05 10:02:28 UTC, after the 10:02:22 UTC commit:

- [Docs](https://github.com/link-foundation/python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/37293968400)
- [Workflows](https://github.com/link-foundation/python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/37293968412)
- [Security](https://github.com/link-foundation/python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/37293968434)

The base branch is an ancestor of this branch, and the working tree is clean. Publishing and Pages deployment jobs are skipped on this pull request as configured.

body:
Fixes #85
Fixes #86
Fixes #87

## Requirements and implementation

| Issue | Requirement | Change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #85 | Use the released numeric version for manual-release changelog headings. | `version_and_commit.py` bumps first, re-reads `project.version`, then passes that value to `scriv collect --version`. The earlier workflow collection step is removed. |
| #85 | Commit version, changelog, and consumed fragments together without duplicate sections. | `bump_version.py --skip-changelog` leaves the detailed entry to Scriv when fragments exist. With no fragments, the existing generic entry remains. The version script stages and commits the complete result. |
| #85 | Make release notes find the new entry. | Correct Scriv's Markdown heading configuration (`md_header_level = 2`, title without heading marks) and accept bracketed and older plain version headings in `create_github_release.py`. |
| #85 | Prevent regression for all bump types. | A local Git remote integration test runs patch, minor, and major releases from `0.1.0`, checks `0.1.1`/`0.2.0`/`1.0.0` headings, confirms fragment consumption and a clean committed tree, and extracts the fragment as release notes. The no-fragment path is covered too. |
| #86 | Update every affected artifact download and guard the pins. | Both package distribution and Docker digest downloads use `actions/download-artifact@v8`; workflow policy tests require two v8 references and reject v7. |
| #87 | Deliver both fixes in one PR with full closing references. | This PR includes both fixes and the three `Fixes` lines above. |

The template remains at its initial `0.1.0` version. Its manual dispatch calculates the next version; a changelog fragment records these changes for that release. The release path itself was not run on a hosted runner in this PR.

## Reproduction and verification

Before the fix, the new tests failed: the version script wrote only a generic changelog entry, the release-note extractor returned `Release 0.1.1` for Scriv headings, and workflow policy still found v7 downloads. A real Scriv integration run also exposed the existing malformed `# ## [version]` heading, which the configuration change corrects.

- Full `pytest` suite passed.
- `ruff check .` and `ruff format --check .` passed.
- `mypy src/` and `python scripts/check_file_size.py` passed.
- The CI-pinned `rhysd/actionlint` v1.7.12 image passed on all workflows.
- `git diff --check` passed.

## Research and alternatives

[Scriv's collect command](https://scriv.readthedocs.io/en/latest/commands.html) accepts an explicit version, and [Scriv's configuration](https://scriv.readthedocs.io/en/latest/configuration.html) separates entry title text from Markdown heading level. `scriv print --version` could replace the existing release-note parser, but the parser now supports both Scriv headings and older plain headings without changing the release command's other behavior.

The upstream [download-artifact v8 release](https://github.com/actions/download-artifact/releases/tag/v8.0.0) adds digest enforcement by default. The template uses ordinary artifacts from the same workflow, so no input change was needed. An [upstream report](https://github.com/actions/upload-artifact/issues/811) has also observed `DEP0005` with v8 during a separate failed download; changing the pin follows #86's requested fix, while absence of that warning in every runner environment cannot be established without a live release run.
